one_month_reasoning: The one scheduled event in the window is Q3 FY2026 earnings. It has not been announced in any filing I read; I infer late October from the Q2 timing (July 29) and last year's Q3 (around Oct 29). Q3 guidance was $270M +/- $10M with non-GAAP EPS of $0.86 +/- $0.09. FormFactor beat the top of its range in Q2, so a beat is likely. Two things cut against an upside reaction. First, Q3 includes a one-time $7-9M IEEPA tariff refund (about 300 bp of gross margin, per the 10-Q). Second, Q4 guidance has to absorb Farmers Branch start-up costs, and management called ~51% the sustainable gross-margin baseline, so Q4 margin guidance probably steps down. The stock has also run about 60% in four weeks (weekly low $92 in the week of Aug 31, close around $149), including +10% on Sep 30 when Deutsche Bank initiated at Buy with a $200 target, citing a second-source position on Nvidia GPU probe cards at TSMC. The post-earnings moves were very large in both directions (+26% after Q2; a sharp drop after Q1). So the distribution is wide (sigma about 25% for the month, slightly above the 85%/3.5 baseline because earnings fall inside the window), with the median nudged a little below spot to $146 for short-term reversal after the run-up and the margin step-down risk. That is roughly neutral, not a strong directional call.

fair_value.method: Blend: forward P/E on my FY2028 EPS of $4.00 x 30 = $120 (weight 0.6); EV/sales on FY2027 revenue of $1.2B x 8 plus ~$0.33B net cash = $125 (0.25); FCF yield on FY2027 FCF of ~$2.00/share at 2.5% = $80 (0.15). Blended about $115, roughly 22% below the $147.90 close.

bear.story: AI/HBM test demand pauses or normalizes in 2027: DRAM is 33% of revenue and SK hynix alone is 24%. Competitors win share (TrendForce expects Technoprobe to overtake FormFactor as #1 in 2026, and HBM competition was flagged on the Q2 call). Gross margin falls back toward the high 40s once tariff refunds and mix tailwinds fade, while Farmers Branch costs land in COGS. EPS of ~$3.00 at 28x is about $85, close to the August-September trading range ($92-105) and below TD Cowen's $100.

base.story: Growth continues but decelerates. Margins hold near the 51% baseline, FY2028 EPS is about $4, and the multiple compresses from ~45x NTM toward ~33-35x as the earnings ramp becomes the expected case. The stock goes roughly sideways from here and ends near the consensus target.

bull.story: The Nvidia/TSMC GPU probe-card second source ramps (Deutsche Bank thesis: ~20% share, >$200M by 2028), HBM4 test intensity lifts DRAM probe revenue, and Farmers Branch pushes gross margin toward 55% early. FY2028 EPS of $5+ at 40x+ takes the stock above Deutsche Bank's $200 target.

thesis_break_reason: A close below ~$90 would break the early-September low ($92) and give back the whole post-Q2 and Deutsche Bank rerating. Given 85% volatility, a move that large most likely reflects a fundamental miss, not noise: a Q4/Q1 guide-down showing the HBM/DRAM or foundry ramp stalling, gross margin falling well below the 51% baseline, the Nvidia second-source opportunity failing, or a large customer (SK hynix 24%, Intel 12%, TSMC 11%) cutting orders.

reasoning: Basic facts come from the Q2 FY2026 8-K and 10-Q. Revenue was $258.2M (+32% y/y), non-GAAP gross margin 53.3%, non-GAAP EPS $0.82, FCF $52.6M. Q3 guide is $270M, 54% gross margin and $0.86 EPS. Net cash is about $335M, with ~78-79M shares, so market cap is about $11.7B at $147.90. The skeptic-lane evidence: (1) The 10-Q shows the Q3 guide includes $7-9M of one-time IEEPA tariff refunds (~300 bp of margin), and management calls ~51% the sustainable gross margin, so the headline Q3 margin overstates the run rate. (2) Concentration: SK hynix is 24% of revenue, and DRAM is 33% of revenue and grew 49% y/y, which is classic peak-cycle exposure. On the Q2 call management mentioned a DRAM mix shift from HBM to DDR and rising HBM competition, and TrendForce expects Technoprobe to overtake FormFactor in 2026. (3) Insiders: the CEO sold in July, August and September 2026 (e.g. ~17.5k shares at $104-106 on Sep 16) and a director sold at $96 on Sep 3. These are small next to his ~467k-share holding and look routine (10b5-1/RSU-related), so I treat them as a mild negative only. (4) Sell-side: consensus target is $133.50, below spot (MarketBeat: 8 Buy/Strong Buy, 4 Hold, 0 Sell). TD Cowen cut to $100 Hold in August, Zacks moved to Hold in July, and AAII rates valuation F at ~102x trailing P/E. (5) There is no short-seller report, litigation or credit stress: debt is about $11M and short interest has been ~3-5% of float. The bear case is valuation and cyclicality, not fraud or solvency. Why the stock jumped on 9/30: no FormFactor 8-K or press release was filed that day (EDGAR list checked). Press reports tie the move to Deutsche Bank initiating at Buy with a $200 target, citing a second-source position on Nvidia GPU probe cards at TSMC (initial sales 2H26, ~20% share, >$200M by 2028). That comes from one sell-side source and is unconfirmed by the company. Price history (weekly): $160 peak in late June, an $82 intraweek low before Q2 earnings, $92 in early September, then ~$149, which confirms 85%-vol behavior. My blended fair value is ~$115 (FY2028 EPS $4 x 30x as the main method), below spot. I don't make that a directional short call, because AI-semi momentum and the plausible Nvidia upside keep a fat right tail. Scenarios: bear $85 (30%), base $138 (45%), bull $215 (25%). The ladder is a mixture of lognormals around those prices (sigma 0.30-0.35 each), giving a median of ~$135 and P(>=$148) of ~0.42, slightly below the probability of a flat outcome. The total spread is consistent with the stock's realized volatility.
